title: Transactional Terraform rollback for VPC healthcheck failures
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Implement a safe, transactional rollback mechanism for Private (VPC) healthcheck failures that integrates with our Terraform IaC flow. The goal is to enable automated, reversible remediation when healthchecks manifest as resource misconfigurations or transient infra failures, while ensuring we never perform a destructive automated change without staged verification. This ticket covers: (1) a 'transactional' pattern for Terraform operations (plan snapshot -> preflight approval gates -> canary apply -> monitor -> promote or rollback), (2) a lightweight state snapshot and compare service to detect drift and revert only the minimal changes, (3) runbook pages and automation hooks for on-call to safely trigger remediation or cancel, and (4) CI/CD safety controls (locks, dry-run diffs, and irreversible-change vetoes).
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible pipeline that performs terraform plan -> plan-snapshot -> gated canary apply -> verification -> promote or rollback
Automated rollback executes within the same IaC transaction window and restores the previous plan snapshot state for the affected resources
Runbook documented with step-by-step failover and manual override procedures and play-tested in staging
Metric hooks and alerts created: canary-failure-sla, rollback-executed, drift-detected, and lock-contention
Automation respects security_review_required and requires SRE approval for destructive change paths
runbook_steps: 1) Alert triage: identify symptom (liveness/readiness/gateway timeout) and affected customer/region
2) Run automated diagnostics: curl endpoints, check node heartbeats, collect 'tf plan' snapshot via runbook-tooling
3) If plan snapshot shows drift on networking or SG rules, mark incident as 'tf-drift-suspected' and trigger canary pipeline
4) Canary pipeline (automated): acquire infra lock -> apply subset of changes to 1 AZ -> run healthcheck probe set for 10 minutes -> if pass, promote -> if fail, automatic rollback to plan snapshot
5) If automatic rollback fails or is blocked, escalate to SRE with runbook logs and an immediate manual rollback play
6) Post-incident: create a minimal Terraform change (rollback patch) and schedule a dry-run in staging with a postmortem tag
tasks: Design transactional agent that manages plan snapshots and apply/rollback orchestration
Add lock manager to Terraform CI job to prevent concurrent mutating runs
Implement canary selector that chooses minimal resource set for staged apply
Wire monitoring hooks: success/failure events, applied plan id, rollback id
Write runbook page and shorthands for on-call to run manual rollback and debug scripts
Integration tests in a dedicated staging VPC that simulate common healthcheck failures
decisions: Use plan snapshot + state diff to define the minimal rollback surface instead of full state restore to minimize blast radius
Canary applies will be single-AZ and limited to non-destructive changes by default; destructive changes require explicit SRE approval
Implement automation as an agent in 'infra' repo (tf-transactional-agent) that calls terraform via wrapper and stores immutable plan artifacts in GCS
Rollback must be idempotent and logged with a unique rollback id to allow audit and replay
We will prevent automated rollback for changes that remove encryption/KMS bindings or RBAC principals; these will require manual approval

notes: Prototype stores plan snapshots as compressed JSON with a SHA256 manifest and timestamp; snapshot IDs are used by the transactional agent
Plan-snapshot -> apply -> post-verify -> promote flow reduces human-in-the-loop for obvious transient drifts (BGP flap, SG mis-ordering)
Fallback options include (a) partial taint+recreate, (b) rollback apply of previous snapshot, (c) manual terraform apply by SRE
We should coordinate with Console team to expose canary state and rollback actions in the Private Console UI for operator convenience
Consider future enhancement: config-driven safe-apply policies per-customer, e.g., allow-auto-rollback: false for high-risk customers
